course_description: This course deepens understanding of Latinx Literature and culture by engaging with a specific topic in Chicanx/Latinx Studies and placing the analysis of literature and other cultural expressions in relation to its political, cultural, and aesthetic developments.
course_notes: This course explores the complex topic of Latinx health, which entails an investigation into the contributing factors to Latinx disease, disability, and pre-mature death and a close attention to Latinx responses to such profound (or sometimes mundane) human conditions. This latter endeavor involves a multi-faceted approach. Reading works such as Gloría Anzaldua¿s short story ¿Puddles,¿ entries from Cherríe Moraga¿s memoir In the Wings, Daisy Hernández¿s The Kissing Bug (investigative journalism/memoir), selections from Jasminne Méndez¿s hybridized collection of essays and poems Night-Blooming Jasmin(n)e, and essays from Aurora Levins Morales¿ Medicine Stories, we will consider where Latinx cultures turn to for healing, how they understand and narrate illness, and how illness challenges them to re-construct their relationships with culture.
